title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

relationships.phenotype: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Paper links homozygous ABCA2 truncating variants to developmental delay/ID, but does not name IDPOGSA or describe poor growth, seizures, or ataxia.

paragraphs.text: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive disorder associated with biallelic truncating variants in ABCA2. Maddirevula et al. (2019) described affected individuals with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, and Aslam and Naz (2019) reported sibs from a consanguineous family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria, a presentation they regarded as an extension of the phenotypic spectrum.

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Autozygome, a rich source of homozygous variants, has been successfully utilized for the high throughput identification of novel autosomal recessive disease genes.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance follows from homozygous variants segregating with the disease within the autozygome framework. The paper doesn't explicitly label the ABCA2 disorder.

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is associated with biallelic truncating variants in ABCA2.
checks.evidence_quote: fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]) and (NM_212533.2:c.1027C>T:p.[Gln343*])
checks.explanation: Homozygous truncating variants are biallelic.

checks.explanation: The abstract describes two affected siblings from a consanguineous family who have an ABCA2 variant and cerebellar ataxia.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) searched a database of 799 research and 1,750 clinical exomes for homozygous likely deleterious variants in genes with tentative disease links. They identified 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. These families carried homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2. The authors considered this phenotype sufficiently different from the previously reported amyotrophic lateral sclerosis to possibly represent a distinct allelic disorder. Facial photographs of the index patient (16DG0071) showed no apparent gross dysmorphism.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) reported 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family who had a movement disorder. Their symptoms were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Magnetic resonance imaging of the older sib showed no brain abnormalities. Low density lipoprotein levels were elevated in blood samples from both affected individuals. The authors noted that the phenotype closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to study patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes. In 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability, they identified homozygous truncating mutations in the ABCA2 gene: c.740dupT (Gly248ArgfsTer38) and c.1027C-T (Gln343Ter). The mutations fully segregated with the disorder in the families.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) performed whole-exome sequencing in 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria. They identified a frameshift mutation in the ABCA2 gene: c.4993delG (Val1665TyrfsTer36). Sanger sequencing showed that the mutation segregated with the disorder. It was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls. The abstract did not state the zygosity of the mutation.

agent.process_note: I read all three files in full: the Maddirevula et al. (2019) full text and the Hu et al. (2019) and Aslam and Naz (2019) abstracts. The Hu et al. abstract does not mention ABCA2, specific families or phenotypes, so I left it uncited. The detailed clinical data for the Maddirevula families are in Supplementary Table 1/Table S1, which is not available. As a result, poor growth and seizures are not documented in the available text. I also could not find the families' ancestry or ages, or which variant occurred in which family. The Aslam and Naz abstract does not state the zygosity of the c.4993delG variant. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the gene's MIM number and chromosomal location are left out of the intro.
